Smugglers don’t rest. Neither do we.

This repeat offender admitted to working as a foot guide for the violent Sinaloa Cartel, smuggling people for $500-$700 per person.

He now faces felony prosecution for alien smuggling (8USC1324) and felony illegal re-entry (8USC1326).

tweets.text:
SEX OFFENDER IN CUSTODY!

Daniel Torres-Rivas, a repeat offender with two arrests for aggravated indecent exposure, was turned over to USBP after serving 365 days in jail. The Salvadoran national recently served time for a 2024 incident where he self-stimulated in public at a retail store in Auburn Hills, MI. Now, he faces prosecution for felony illegal re-entry (8USC1326), inadmissible alien (8USC1182), and previously removed alien (212a9Aii).

This is why immigration detainers are vital to removing these bad actors from our communities.

STASH HOUSES SHUT DOWN
4/3- U.S. Border Patrol agents in the El Paso Sector shut down two stash houses operating in local neighborhoods. A total of 25 illegal aliens were taken into custody, including two unaccompanied children.

Among those arrested, two smugglers are now facing prosecution for alien smuggling (8USC1324), felony illegal re-entry (8USC1326), and improper entry (8USC1325). Thats not it, 7 illegal aliens now face prosecution for felony illegal re-entry to include a foot guide.

The message is clear- consequences will be delivered to ALL individuals entering the country illegally.

On 4/8, USBP agents in San Diego seized over 223 lbs. of dangerous drugs.

I-8 Checkpoint: Agents uncovered 78 vacuum-sealed packages of meth hidden throughout a vehicle. They arrested two individuals now facing federal charges for drug possession (21 USC 841) and importation (21 USC 952).

San Clemente, CA: A vehicle stop on I-5 led agents to 25 cocaine-filled packages stashed in the trunk. The driver was arrested and faces state charges for possession with intent to distribute (11351 HS).

Every stop, every seizure—saving lives and protecting communities.

🔹vehicle tampering
🔹disorderly conduct
🔹battery

He was ordered removed by an immigration judge- he now faces prosecution for felony illegal re-entry (8USC1326) and his removal order was reinstated.

tweets.text:
LIQUID METH SEIZED!

On 4/8, USBP agents in Murrieta, CA, stopped an 18-wheeler after a suspicious story and a nervous driver raised red flags. A K9 team alerted to narcotics odors coming from the vehicle, prompting a deeper inspection. Agents discovered hidden compartments inside both diesel tanks—packed with 761 pounds of liquid meth. The driver now faces federal charges for distributing a controlled substance (21 USC 841).

So far in FY25, USBP agents and law enforcement partners have seized over 10,000 pounds of meth—a testament to their vigilance and commitment.

FIREARMS SMUGGLING!

USBP agents in Indio, CA intercepted a weapons and ammunition smuggling attempt during a traffic stop—thanks to an alert from a Border Patrol K-9.

Agents searched the vehicle and uncovered bulk ammunition, a machine gun, a handgun, and various firearm parts—all hidden within the vehicle’s structure. The driver, a U.S. citizen and convicted felon, now faces charges for being a felon in possession of a firearm (18 USC 922) and firearms trafficking (18 USC 933a1).

On April 9, USBP agents in Yuma, AZ, stopped a human smuggling attempt. Agents arrested one smuggler and five illegal aliens after a failed vehicle bailout.  The driver made several desperate attempts to evade arrest, but agents stayed on him. The vehicle eventually stopped, and all six individuals bailed out—but they didn’t get far. Agents quickly apprehended every one of them. 

The driver now faces prosecution for felony alien smuggling under 8 USC 1324. The five Mexican nationals are being charged as inadmissible aliens under 8 USC 1182.
